cr_data.provenance:
[1] By February 25, 1958, (The Downtown Gallery, New York, New York, USA); [2] June 28, 1960, purchased by Allen-Bradley Co. (Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA); 3] June 1969, gift to The Bradley Family Foundation (Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA); 1977, gift to Milwaukee Art Center (Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA) 
NOTES: 
[1] Downtown Gallery, Georgia O’Keeffe: Watercolors, 1916–17 (New York: The Downtown Gallery, 1958), cat. 52. 
[2] Invoice addressed to The Allen-Bradley Company in MAM object file, marked paid by “AB” in July 1960. See also Barbara Buhler Lynes, Georgia O'Keeffe: Catalogue Raisonné. Vol. 1 (New Haven: Yale University Press, 1999), p. 129, cat. 234. 
[3] Documentation from The Bradley Family Foundation in MAM object file. See also Barbara Buhler Lynes, Georgia O'Keeffe: Catalogue Raisonné. Vol. 1 (New Haven: Yale University Press, 1999), p. 129, cat. 234. 
(Source: MAM, 2025)
remarks_1999: Not recorded Whitney Archive. Abiquiú Notebooks indicates, "Red, blue, and cerise." Abiquiú Notebooks after 1977 indicates, "Sold by Halpert." Because O'Keeffe encouraged male students to finish the school term before joining the war effort in 1916 and 1917, she was seen as unpatriotic by her colleagues at the West Texas State Normal College. Inspired by this issue. Completed in San Antonio, on basis of Stieglitz–O'Keeffe correspondence. (Source: Lynes, 1999)
